deep.reconstruction:
This page has no derivation. It is a run of methodological aphorisms from Hilbert's notebook on how to do mathematics and on the structure of mathematical physics. It belongs to the same series as the neighbouring pages: the pages on axiomatics versus single principles, on the division of labour, and on 'reducing the infinite to the finite'. In order:

(1) Working maxim. 'Given the abundance of things seen, try to forget and ignore what is superfluous, so that you have the essential ready at every moment and do not lose sight of the direct path to the goal.' 'das Ziel' is underlined.

(2) The faculties needed for productive mathematics. Imagination (Phantasie) is the main thing. In addition one needs enough willpower and memory to gain mastery over formalism and the technique of calculation.

(3) The two limiting passages of mathematical physics.
- From the continuous to the discontinuous: mechanics of continua. The inserted, circled gloss 'indem man allmälige Übergänge rascher und plötzlicher nimmt' (making gradual transitions faster and more abrupt) describes this passage most naturally, as with shocks and discontinuities obtained as limits of steep smooth transitions. Note that the gloss is physically placed in the second parenthesis.
- From the discontinuous to the continuous: by taking mean values, as in molecular physics. In modern terms this is the continuum or hydrodynamic limit of particle systems, i.e. kinetic theory to continuum mechanics.

(4) Reconciliation of the continuum method and the atomistic method. Neither can be fruitful without the other; they complement each other and merge. 'The continuum method gives the direction, atomism the deeper understanding.'

(5) The 'method of continuity' in mathematics. It teaches that whatever one knows can be extended by clever arrangement, so that one always knows something more. Hence 'the set of knowledge (Wissensmenge) is not a closed set in mathematics'. This is a metaphorical use of the topological or set-theoretic notion of closedness.

(6) Start of a classification. Physics falls into three parts:
1. fundamental differential equations, (a) by the continuum method, (b) by the atomic method;
2. preparation ('Zubereitung') of the differential equations.
The sentence continues on the page supplied as 'previous': specialisation, limiting cases, and 3. integration (ordinary and partial). The folio order of the context pages therefore appears reversed relative to reading order.

Nothing is computed. Point (3) and point (4) are the content of the second half of Hilbert's 6th Paris problem (1900): the limiting processes leading from the atomistic view to the laws of motion of continua, following Boltzmann.
errors: No mathematical errors: the page contains no calculations.

Possible misplacement of the inserted gloss. 'Making gradual transitions faster and more abrupt' logically illustrates the passage continuous to discontinuous (the first case), yet it is written inside the second parenthesis, which ends with 'Nehmen von Mittelwerten'. Either Hilbert inserted it at the wrong spot, or it is meant as an alternative mechanism. This is an interpretive point, not a mathematical error.

results.what: Two complementary limiting procedures in mathematical physics: continuum to discontinuity (abrupt transitions) and atomistic to continuum (averaging), with a call for their reconciliation
results.modern_name: Continuum / hydrodynamic limit of particle systems (kinetic theory to continuum mechanics); Hilbert's 6th problem, second part
results.usually_credited_to: Boltzmann (kinetic theory); posed as a programme by Hilbert in the 6th Paris problem (1900); Hilbert 1912 (Boltzmann equation, Hilbert expansion)

results.what: Mathematical knowledge as a 'non-closed set' extendable by the method of continuity
results.modern_name: Philosophical aphorism; cf. Hilbert's optimism about the solvability of every problem
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert (general views, e.g. 1900 Paris address, 1930 Königsberg address)

results.what: Imagination as the main faculty in mathematics, supplemented by will and memory to master formal technique
results.usually_credited_to: Commonplace (Weierstrass, Poincaré, Hilbert all expressed similar views)

results.what: Tripartite division of physics: fundamental differential equations (continuum vs atomic), their preparation (specialisation, limiting cases), their integration
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert's lectures on mathematical physics and axiomatization of physics

deep.surprise_reason: Purely reflective notes with no new mathematics. The continuum/atomism theme is precisely the publicly stated content of Hilbert's 6th problem and his later kinetic-theory work. The aphorisms are of biographical interest only.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Fülle der Gesichte' matches the image; 'das Ziel' is underlined in the original.
'Kein kann ohne die andere' – the image reads 'Kein kann' (presumably intended 'Keine kann').

The circled insertion 'indem man allmäligen Uebergänge rascher und plötzlicher nimmt' is written on its own line between '(durch' and 'Nehmen von Mittelwerten'. A struck-out word (looks like 'Diff' or a scribble) sits to its left. Its logical attachment to the first case (continuous to discontinuous) is uncertain.
Final line 'Zubereitung der Diffe.' continues as 'rentialgl.' on the page given as 'previous', so the context pages appear to be in reversed order.
